title: Fluorescent Western Protocol
author: Steven J Burgess
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.b3q6qmze

steps.title: Maintain membranes in dark box
steps.instruction: Keep all membranes in the black Western blot incubation box for every step; after adding secondary antibody protect from light. Clean the box thoroughly between uses; if background increases, wipe with 70 % ethanol and dry completely.

steps.title: Rinse membrane with deionized water
steps.instruction: Rinse the membrane with de‑ionized (dH₂O) water.

steps.title: Block membrane with Intercept buffer
steps.instruction: Block nonspecific binding using Intercept (PBS) Blocking Buffer (LI‑COR Catalog #927‑70001) for 1 hour at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Discard any residual PBS before adding blocking buffer.
Incubate membrane in ~15 mL blocking solution (15 mL 1× PBS + 0.75 g non‑fat dry milk) at RT for 01:00:00.
Alternative blocking buffer: PBS with 5 % w/v milk powder (no Tween‑20).
Do NOT use milk powder as a blocker if the target protein is phosphorylated.

steps.title: Incubate membrane with primary antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate the blocked membrane with primary antibody diluted in Intercept® T20 (PBS) Antibody Diluent (LI‑COR Catalog #927‑75001).

substeps.instruction: Prepare dilution (typical 1:2,000–1:5,000) in ~15 mL diluent (15 mL 1× PBST + 0.75 g non‑fat dry milk).
Incubate overnight (≈16 h) at 4 °C with gentle agitation on a platform shaker set to 50 rpm.
Alternative diluent: PBST (0.1 % Tween‑20, 5 % milk).
Empirically determine the optimal dilution for each antibody.

steps.title: Prepare 1 L PBS‑T solution
steps.instruction: Dilute 100 mL of 10× PBS with distilled water to a final volume of 1 L to make 1 L of PBS‑T.

steps.title: Remove primary antibody and wash
steps.instruction: Discard the primary antibody solution and wash the membrane with PBS‑T.

substeps.instruction: Collect the used primary antibody in a tube and store at –20 °C if it will be reused.

steps.title: PBS‑T wash series (3×10 min)
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane with PBS‑T three times.

substeps.instruction: Cover membrane with PBS‑T.
Shake vigorously on a platform shaker at 50 rpm, room temperature, for 10 minutes.
Repeat the above wash two more times (total 3 washes).
If high background is observed, increase each wash to 20 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare secondary antibody dilution
steps.instruction: Make a working dilution of the secondary antibody using Intercept® T20 (PBS) Antibody Diluent (LI‑COR Catalog #927‑75001).

substeps.instruction: For PVDF membranes add 0.01 % SDS to the diluent.
Microcentrifuge the secondary antibody and transfer the clear supernatant to avoid protein complexes.
Typical dilution is 1:20,000 in ~15 mL diluent (15 mL 1× PBST + 0.75 g non‑fat dry milk).
Alternative diluent: PBST (0.1 % Tween‑20, 5 % milk).
Adjust dilution empirically based on antibody and sample.

steps.title: Incubate membrane with secondary antibody
steps.instruction: Incubate the membrane with the prepared secondary antibody for 1 hour at room temperature with gentle agitation on a platform shaker.

substeps.instruction: Do not exceed 1 hour; longer incubations increase background.

steps.title: Remove secondary antibody and rinse
steps.instruction: Discard the secondary antibody solution and rinse the membrane with distilled water to eliminate residual blocking agent.

steps.title: Post‑secondary PBS‑T wash
steps.instruction: Wash the membrane with PBS‑T after secondary incubation.

substeps.instruction: Cover membrane with PBS‑T.
Agitate at 80 rpm, room temperature, for 10 minutes.
If high background, increase wash time to 20 minutes.
Discard PBS‑T and repeat this wash three additional times (total of four washes).
More washes (up to five or more) can be performed to further reduce background.

steps.title: Final PBS rinse
steps.instruction: Rinse the membrane and then cover it with 1× PBS, agitate at 80 rpm, room temperature, for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Image blot on Odyssey CLx
steps.instruction: Image the blot using the LI‑COR Odyssey CLx imaging system. Before imaging, clean the Odyssey platform thoroughly with isopropanol to remove any residual protein from previous blots.
